question.text: The winding-up section of the PPM for Sharavathi Timber Fund describes the process for dissolving the AIF. Which of the following triggers winding up under SEBI AIF Regulations?

answer.text: A single investor requesting the fund be wound up
A 5% decline in the fund's NAV from its peak

Expiry of the fund's tenure, the trustees or trustee company being of the opinion that the scheme should be wound up in investors' interests, a 75%-by-value investor resolution to wind up, or a SEBI direction to do so
The fund manager attending a competitor's investor conference

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists the winding-up triggers as: expiry of the scheme's tenure; the trustees or trustee company forming the opinion that winding up is in the investors' interests; a resolution passed by 75% of investors by value to wind up; or a direction from SEBI. After winding up, the scheme enters the liquidation period and may use in-specie distribution, liquidation schemes, and a dissolution period. A single investor cannot force winding up, NAV decline is ordinary market risk, and the last option is absurd. The Trap: A single-investor request confuses individual redemption rights (which do not exist in close-ended AIFs) with the collective triggers requiring trustee opinion, supermajority investor consent, or SEBI direction. Note: Aligned the keyed option to the source-listed triggers (tenure expiry, trustee opinion, 75% investor resolution, SEBI direction). Removed the unsupported 'achievement of fund objectives / all investments realised' language and the pro-tip claim of a 12-24 month liquidation timeline.
